answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a $1,000 bond for 90 days before bidding, with proven fraud triggering forfeiture. Creating 100 sybils therefore ties up $100,000, even if the attacker uses them only once. Reputation can rise from nadir to summit, but every new identity must post its own bond; the fable of limitless free identities fails because multiplying accounts multiplies capital costs.
